title: Ornette on tenor and Ornette with Coltrane's rhythm section
summary: He admires Ornette's tenor playing and a tune of his that quotes it, and notes Ornette brought Trane's rhythm section to his own music.

blocks.x: What did you think about Ornette on tenor?

I dug Ornette on tenor. Matter of fact I wrote on my new record we have this song called “Whiplashing”, the first notes of my solo are the first four notes on the song “Eos.” Just the same thing Ornette played. He wasn’t a good tenor player, but again, he was just using the tenor as the medium. And when he played tenor, it completely changed the character of the songs in a way that, had he played that on alto, it wouldn’t have sounded that way.
Talking about Ornette and going back to the Coltrane axis. Yeah, Coltrane played with Ornette’s rhythm section, but then Ornette played with Trane’s rhythm section….(interrupted)
Oh yeah, but Ornette played with Trane’s rhythm section, but he brought them to his thing.

When you listen to records like New York is Now and all that…. Whew! But he brought them to his thing. You know what I mean. He wasn’t trying to get to Trane’s thing. He just said, “Alright, let’s do it.” You know, man, that’s a great record, too. With Dewey, yeah that’s killin’ man.
